title: Mapping and Counting High-Intensity Perineuronal Nets in the Somatosensory Cortex
author: Dana Layo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcf8itrw

steps.title: Prepare Software and Files
steps.instruction: Ensure all necessary software and data are available on the computer.

substeps.instruction: Download ImageJ from the NIH.
Obtain 10x whole somatosensory cortex images (sagittal directions) containing the dentate gyrus and striatum.
Obtain a digital copy of the mouse atlas.
Determine the measured equivalent of a pixel from the microscope using the 10x objective.

steps.title: Calibrate ImageJ Scale
steps.instruction: Set the spatial scale in ImageJ to match the microscope objective.

substeps.instruction: Open an image in ImageJ.
Navigate to Analyze -> Set Scale.
Insert the measurement values from the microscope.
Check 'Global' and click out of the image.
When opening subsequent images, ensure 'deactivate global calibration' is unchecked to maintain parameters.

steps.title: Align Map to Fluorescent Image
steps.instruction: Overlay the anatomical map onto the fluorescent image and align them.

substeps.instruction: Open the corresponding map image in ImageJ.
Overlay the map onto the fluorescent image via Image -> Overlay -> Add Image; select the appropriate map.
Set the map opacity to approximately 20% to see the underlying image.
Add the overlay to the ROI Manager (Image -> Overlay -> To ROI Manager).
Fit the map to the cortex. To rotate the fluorescent image, deselect the map and go to Image -> Rotate, inserting the desired degrees.
Reselect and drag the map until the curve of the striatum and the front edge of the hippocampus line up, and the front of the tissue aligns with the map.

steps.title: Flatten and Save Aligned Image
steps.instruction: Create a single flattened image of the overlay for reference.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Image -> Overlay -> Flatten.
Save the result as a tiff (File -> Save As) in the original image folder, naming it with 'flatten' and the degree of rotation.
Keep this flattened image open in ImageJ.

steps.title: Define Somatosensory Cortex Area
steps.instruction: Outline and measure the total somatosensory cortex area.

substeps.instruction: Increase image brightness/contrast (Image -> Adjust -> Brightness/Contrast) to visualize the striatum and hippocampus borders.
Use the polygon tool to outline the whole somatosensory cortex, double-clicking the final point to close the loop.
Press 't' to save the outline to the ROI Manager.
Rename the ROI as 'SS1 Area'.
Select 'Measure' in the ROI Manager to record the area value.
Save the ROI (ROI Manager -> More -> Save) in the original image folder.

steps.title: Define Somatosensory Subregions
steps.instruction: Outline and measure individual primary somatosensory subregions.

substeps.instruction: Increase brightness/contrast to see borders clearly.
Use the polygon tool to outline one subregion at a time, double-clicking to close the outline.
Press 't' to save each outline to the ROI Manager.
Rename each ROI as '(Subregion) Area' immediately.
Use 'show all' in the ROI Manager to ensure subregion borders do not overlap.
Save each ROI as an individual file (ROI Manager -> More -> Save) in the original image folder.
Select 'Measure' in the ROI Manager to record the area values for all subregions.

steps.title: Count High-Intensity PNNs
steps.instruction: Quantify PNNs within each subregion using the original fluorescent images.

substeps.instruction: Open the original fluorescent image and rotate it (Image -> Transform -> Rotate) according to the rotation degree noted in the flattened image name.
Drag the subregion area ROI file into ImageJ and press 't' to open it in the ROI Manager.
Ensure 'show all' is checked in the ROI Manager.
Maximize contrast using Image -> Adjust -> Brightness/Contrast; note the initial values and use 'reset' periodically to maintain accuracy.
Identify High-Intensity PNNs (must be at least 80% complete; can be filled-in circles or donut-shaped).
Count PNNs by clicking on them with the point tool and pressing 't' to save each to the ROI Manager.
Save PNN counts: In ROI Manager, press 'deselect', then go to More -> Save and name the file 'subregion PNN' in the original image folder.
Record the total count by selecting 'deselect' then 'Measure' in the ROI Manager.

steps.title: Iterate Process
steps.instruction: Repeat the counting process for every subregion.
